boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain University of Alabama at Birmingham
boards.description: Ten currently documented food stops on or near the UAB medical district, with late availability noted from direct sources.

cards.title: WOW Wings Late Nite
cards.subtitle: McMahon Food Hall, UAB
cards.notes: Order through the Everyday app, then use the McMahon Food Hall pickup location during its documented evening service window.
cards.short_summary: A campus pickup option with service through midnight Wednesday–Sunday.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB Student Affairs states that WOW Wings Late Nite operates Wednesday–Sunday from 4:00 PM to 12:00 AM.
cards.source_title: Late Night Dining/New Location-McMahon Food Hall
cards.access_notes: Documented hours: Wednesday–Sunday, 4:00 PM–12:00 AM. Order through the Everyday app; pickup is at McMahon Food Hall.

cards.title: Vocelli Pizza at Camp Hall
cards.subtitle: 1516 10th Ave S, Camp Hall first floor
cards.notes: Use the Camp Hall location for a late pizza pickup or delivery option; confirm availability in the ordering channel before heading over.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus pizza counter with delivery listed until midnight.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB Dining lists Vocelli Pizza at Camp Hall with delivery until 12:00 AM daily; its dining room closes earlier.
cards.access_notes: UAB lists delivery until 12:00 AM daily. Dining room closes at 10:00 PM Sunday–Thursday and 10:30 PM Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: Starbucks Coffee, North Pavilion
cards.subtitle: UAB Hospital North Pavilion, second floor
cards.notes: For a weekday late stop inside the medical district, use the North Pavilion second-floor full-service Starbucks before the listed midnight close.
cards.short_summary: A hospital-campus coffee shop with midnight weekday hours.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB Hospital’s 2026 patient guide lists Starbucks on the North Pavilion second floor open Monday–Friday from 5:00 AM to 12:00 AM.
cards.access_notes: Documented hours: Monday–Friday, 5:00 AM–12:00 AM; Saturday–Sunday, 8:00 AM–6:00 PM. Located on North Pavilion’s second floor.

cards.title: Panera Bread, North Pavilion
cards.subtitle: UAB Hospital North Pavilion, second floor
cards.notes: Use the North Pavilion second-floor Panera for an evening meal on a weekday; weekend service ends earlier, so check the day first.
cards.short_summary: A UAB Hospital food option documented until 10 PM on weekdays.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB Hospital’s 2026 patient guide lists Panera Bread on the North Pavilion second floor open Monday–Friday from 6:00 AM to 10:00 PM.
cards.access_notes: Documented hours: Monday–Friday, 6:00 AM–10:00 PM; Saturday–Sunday, 10:00 AM–6:30 PM. North Pavilion second floor.

cards.title: Bistro on the Pavilion
cards.subtitle: UAB Hospital North Pavilion Food Court
cards.notes: Head to the North Pavilion Food Court for the named bistro when you need a documented on-site option after typical dinner hours.
cards.short_summary: A hospital food-court counter listed through 1 AM every day.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB Hospital’s 2026 patient guide lists Bistro on the Pavilion open 11:00 AM to 1:00 AM every day.
cards.access_notes: Documented hours: 11:00 AM–1:00 AM every day. Located in the North Pavilion Food Court on the second floor.

cards.title: McDonald's on 5th Avenue South
cards.subtitle: 1501 5th Ave S, Birmingham
cards.notes: Use the drive-thru when you need the latest documented access; the restaurant lobby has earlier midnight closing hours.
cards.short_summary: A nearby drive-thru listed as open 24 hours daily.
cards.evidence_claim: McDonald’s lists the 1501 5th Avenue South drive-thru as open 24 hours daily; restaurant and lobby hours run to midnight.
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru: open 24 hours daily. Restaurant and lobby: 5:00 AM–12:00 AM daily.

cards.title: Taco Bell on 7th Avenue South
cards.subtitle: 2124 7th Ave S, Birmingham
cards.notes: Plan this as a drive-thru or takeout stop after the dining room closes; the published drive-thru schedule runs into early morning.
cards.short_summary: A nearby Taco Bell with drive-thru service documented as late as 4 AM.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists its 2124 7th Avenue South drive-thru open until 4:00 AM Wednesday–Saturday and until 3:00 AM Sunday–Tuesday.
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru: until 4:00 AM Wednesday–Saturday; until 3:00 AM Sunday–Tuesday. The listed dine-in hours end at 10:00 PM.

cards.title: Ruscelli's
cards.subtitle: 2801 7th Ave S, Birmingham
cards.notes: Use the published late-night schedule to time pickup or delivery, and confirm the day because Monday is listed as closed.
cards.short_summary: A Southside pizza restaurant with service as late as 2 AM on selected nights.
cards.evidence_claim: Ruscelli’s lists late-night hours until 2:00 AM Tuesday–Saturday, with Sunday service until 12:00 AM.
cards.access_notes: Late-night hours: Tuesday–Thursday 9:00 PM–2:00 AM; Friday–Saturday 5:00 PM–2:00 AM; Sunday 5:00 PM–12:00 AM; Monday closed.

cards.title: The Purple Onion Lakeview
cards.subtitle: 737 29th St S, Birmingham
cards.notes: Use the online ordering page to verify the current closing time and place a pickup or delivery order before making the trip.
cards.short_summary: A Lakeview deli and grill whose ordering page lists service until 3:45 AM.
cards.evidence_claim: The Purple Onion Lakeview’s direct online ordering page lists the location at 737 29th Street South as closing at 3:45 AM.
cards.source_title: The Purple Onion Lakeview online ordering
cards.access_notes: The direct ordering page lists 737 29th St S and says it closes at 3:45 AM; verify current ordering availability before departure.

cards.title: Al's Deli & Grill
cards.subtitle: 1629 10th Ave S, Birmingham
cards.notes: Use Al’s when you need an independent food stop near campus; check the day-specific close before leaving, since its schedule varies.
cards.short_summary: A Five Points-area deli and grill documented with late service every day.
cards.evidence_claim: Apple Maps lists Al’s Deli & Grill at 1629 10th Avenue South open until midnight Sunday–Wednesday, 2:00 AM Thursday and Saturday, and 3:00 AM Friday.
cards.source_title: Al's Deli & Grill on Apple Maps
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: until 12:00 AM Sunday–Wednesday, 2:00 AM Thursday and Saturday, and 3:00 AM Friday. Confirm before visiting.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten documented UAB places for studying, connecting, recreation, campus events, and student support.

cards.title: UAB Campus Green
cards.subtitle: Central campus green space
cards.notes: Use the open lawn as a meetup point or check the campus calendar for fairs, performances, and student-organization events before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A campus gathering lawn that hosts student activities and university events.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB describes Campus Green as an open space for the university community and lists student-facing events there, including Connect Fest.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space; check the calendar and reservation rules for scheduled events.

cards.title: Performance Lounge
cards.subtitle: Hill Student Center
cards.notes: Set up for a group project, independent work, or a between-class break; the stage area may be reserved only for public events.
cards.short_summary: A Hill Student Center lounge for study, group work, breaks, and small public performances.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB says the Performance Lounge is used for studying, group projects, relaxing between classes, and small public performances.
cards.access_notes: The wooden stage is reserved for public events and is not reservable by outside groups.

cards.title: Game Room
cards.subtitle: Hill Student Center
cards.notes: Bring your ONE Card and use the staffed Game Room for an on-campus activity break; follow posted equipment and sign-in procedures.
cards.short_summary: A student-only gaming space with published daytime and evening operating hours.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB's Game Room policy states that only active UAB students may use the space and must present a ONE Card for entry.
cards.access_notes: Active UAB students only; hours and capacity limits are posted by Hill Student Center.

cards.title: Off-Campus Student Lounge
cards.subtitle: Hill Student Center, Suite 140
cards.notes: If you commute, use this dedicated lounge to study, eat a meal, socialize, or decompress between classes during its posted weekday hours.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated Hill Student Center lounge for off-campus students between classes.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB states that the lounge is designed for off-campus students to study, socialize, eat meals, and lounge between classes.
cards.source_title: Off-Campus Student Lounge | UAB Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: Intended for off-campus students; UAB lists Monday–Thursday 8 a.m.–6 p.m. and Friday 8 a.m.–5 p.m.

cards.title: Mervyn H. Sterne Library
cards.subtitle: 917 13th St. S.
cards.notes: Choose an open study area, a quiet third-floor seat, or a reservable room; use the HUB Desk and your ONE Card when required.
cards.short_summary: UAB's undergraduate-focused library with quiet, open, individual, and group study options.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB's catalog identifies Sterne as an undergraduate activity hub with group rooms, single carrels, open study areas, and a quiet third-floor area.
cards.access_notes: Room reservations and some study spaces require a valid UAB ONE Card; check in at the HUB Desk when applicable.

cards.entity_name: Lister Hill Library of the Health Sciences
cards.title: Lister Hill Library of the Health Sciences
cards.subtitle: 1700 University Blvd.
cards.notes: Reserve a room for a short solo or collaborative session, then check in at the HUB Service Desk with the required UAB credentials.
cards.short_summary: A health-sciences library with reservable individual and group study rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB Libraries lists 19 Lister Hill study rooms for current UAB community members' collaborative or individual study sessions.
cards.access_notes: For current UAB students and community members; same-day to two-week-ahead reservations and HUB check-in apply.

cards.title: Vulcan Materials Academic Success Center
cards.subtitle: Sterne Library, second floor
cards.notes: Make an appointment or stop by to connect with academic coaching, tutoring, supplemental instruction, and major-exploration support.
cards.short_summary: A Sterne Library academic-support center for UAB undergraduates.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB describes VMASC as a student-centered, peer-led tutoring and small-group instruction center in Sterne Library Room 222.
cards.source_title: Study smarter, not harder: Strategies for a smooth exam week | UAB Reporter
cards.access_notes: Located in Sterne Library Room 222; appointment availability and services vary by program.

cards.title: Campus Recreation Center
cards.subtitle: 1501 University Blvd.
cards.notes: Plan an active break around the pool, courts, fitness areas, track, or climbing wall, and confirm eligibility and facility policies first.
cards.short_summary: A large campus recreation facility with fitness, aquatics, courts, track, and climbing facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB lists a fitness center, pool, climbing and bouldering wall, courts, studios, and other recreation amenities at the Campus Recreation Center.
cards.source_title: Campus Recreation Center | UAB University Recreation
cards.access_notes: Access and participation are governed by UAB University Recreation membership and facility policies.

cards.title: UAB Mini Park
cards.subtitle: Corner of University Blvd. and 14th St. S.
cards.notes: Use this named outdoor stop as a campus meeting point, and have a registered student organization reserve it when planning an event or table.
cards.short_summary: A named UAB outdoor space available to student organizations through campus event reservations.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB Student Affairs includes UAB Mini Park among the spaces student organizations may reserve.
cards.access_notes: Student-organization reservations require access to UAB's online reservation system and may have additional rules.

cards.title: Alys Stephens Center
cards.subtitle: UAB arts venue
cards.notes: Look at the performance calendar and student-ticket details before choosing a show; UAB has documented discounted student tickets for many presented performances.
cards.short_summary: UAB's performing-arts venue, with documented student discounts for many presented shows.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB reported that the Alys Stephens Center offers $10 student tickets to most performances it presents, subject to limited availability.
cards.source_title: UAB students: Get $10 tickets to shows at the Alys Stephens Center | UAB News
cards.access_notes: Ticket availability, pricing, and eligibility vary by performance; consult the current event listing before attending.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-admission places and scheduled activities on or near UAB for an under-21-friendly outing.

cards.title: UAB Campus Green
cards.subtitle: UAB campus, 9th Ave S
cards.notes: Bring a blanket or a classmate and use the open lawn during a listed free Campus Green activity; check the calendar before heading over.
cards.short_summary: An open campus lawn with free scheduled community activities.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB describes Campus Green as open space for the university community and guests, and its calendar lists free activities there.
cards.access_notes: Use the calendar listing to confirm a free activity and any event-specific requirements.

cards.entity_name: Abroms-Engel Institute for the Visual Arts
cards.title: Browse AEIVA exhibitions
cards.subtitle: 1221 10th Ave S, UAB campus
cards.notes: Walk through the contemporary exhibitions together during public hours, then use the displayed work as a prompt for an unhurried conversation.
cards.short_summary: UAB’s contemporary-art center offers rotating public exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: AEIVA states that its exhibitions and programs are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Visit | Abroms-Engel Institute for the Visual Arts
cards.access_notes: Public hours are Tuesday–Saturday, noon–5 p.m.; exhibitions rotate, so check what is on view.

cards.title: See student work at Gallery 501
cards.subtitle: 501 Building, 501 12th St S
cards.notes: Stop in during staffed hours to look at work by UAB art students and invited artists; pair it with a walk through the nearby arts campus.
cards.short_summary: A small UAB gallery centered on student and guest-artist exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB states that Gallery 501 exhibitions and programs are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Gallery 501 | UAB Department of Art and Art History
cards.access_notes: Staffed Monday and Wednesday 2:30–5 p.m. and Friday 2–5 p.m.; appointments are also available.

cards.entity_name: Dennis G. Pappas Historical Collections Gallery
cards.title: Explore the Pappas Gallery
cards.subtitle: Lister Hill Library, 1700 University Blvd
cards.notes: Use the rotating historical displays for a low-key visit, and ask a museum guide for highlights if your group has five or fewer people.
cards.short_summary: A free UAB historical-collections gallery inside Lister Hill Library.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB Libraries says the Pappas Gallery is always free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Visit Us | Dennis G. Pappas Historical Collections Gallery
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Saturday, noon–5 p.m. Non-UAB visitors use the video intercom for library access.

cards.title: Wander the Birmingham Museum of Art
cards.subtitle: 2000 Reverend Abraham Woods Jr Blvd
cards.notes: Meet in the collection galleries and pick one artwork each to discuss; general admission covers the galleries and most exhibitions.
cards.short_summary: A downtown art museum with free general admission.
cards.evidence_claim: The Birmingham Museum of Art states that general admission is free every day and includes collection galleries and most exhibitions.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | Birmingham Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Check the museum page for current hours and any exception for a particular exhibition or closure.

cards.title: Take a Railroad Park loop
cards.subtitle: 1600 1st Ave S, downtown Birmingham
cards.notes: Walk the paths, use the rail trail, or bring your own picnic and settle near the lawns; keep the plan simple and purchase-free.
cards.short_summary: A 19-acre downtown greenspace with paths and open gathering areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Railroad Park states that it is free to the public and open daily.
cards.access_notes: The park lists daily hours of 7 a.m.–11 p.m.; separately priced food or events are optional.

cards.title: Stroll Birmingham Botanical Gardens
cards.subtitle: 2612 Lane Park Rd, Birmingham
cards.notes: Choose a garden section, follow the paths at your own pace, and bring water instead of planning around the café or gift shop.
cards.short_summary: A public garden with walking paths, water features, and free entry.
cards.evidence_claim: Birmingham Botanical Gardens states that general admission is free and the gardens are open to the public every day.
cards.access_notes: Garden grounds are open daily; the official visit page also states parking is free.

cards.title: Hike Red Mountain Park
cards.subtitle: 2011 Frankfurt Dr, Birmingham
cards.notes: Pick a marked trail or overlook, stay on the designated route, and check conditions before leaving; no admission or parking payment is required.
cards.short_summary: A large Birmingham park with trails, overlooks, and mining-history landscape.
cards.evidence_claim: Jefferson County Greenways states that Red Mountain Park has no parking or admission fee.
cards.source_title: Red Mountain Park | Jefferson County Greenways
cards.access_notes: Listed daily hours are 7 a.m.–7 p.m.; use the official trail map and observe posted closures.

cards.title: Visit the Civil Rights National Monument
cards.subtitle: A.G. Gaston Motel area, 1510 5th Ave N
cards.notes: Use the monument’s visitor information to orient your walk through the district and reflect on Birmingham’s civil-rights history together.
cards.short_summary: A National Park Service site interpreting Birmingham’s civil-rights history.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service states that Birmingham Civil Rights National Monument is fee-free year-round and requires no entrance fee or pass.
cards.source_title: Basic Information - Birmingham Civil Rights National Monument
cards.access_notes: The NPS notes that the 1954 wing of the A.G. Gaston Motel is temporarily closed for renovations; use current visitor information.

cards.title: Walk Kelly Ingram Park
cards.subtitle: 5th Ave N & 16th St, Civil Rights District
cards.notes: Follow the short walking trail and pause at the civil-rights monuments; treat the space as a reflective outdoor visit rather than a rushed photo stop.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor civil-rights memorial park with monuments and a short trail.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service lists Kelly Ingram Park as an outdoor green space with civil-rights monuments and a short walking trail; the monument site is fee-free.
cards.source_title: Operating Hours & Seasons - Birmingham Civil Rights National Monument
cards.access_notes: NPS lists the park as open daily from 8 a.m.–8 p.m.; it is an outdoor space, so plan for weather.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten current UAB library-based study environments, selected for their documented quiet, collaboration, reservation, or accessibility features.

cards.entity_name: Mervyn H. Sterne Library First-Floor Collaborative Study Space
cards.title: Sterne First-Floor Collaborative Study Space
cards.subtitle: Mervyn H. Sterne Library, first floor
cards.notes: Set up for a partner session on the first floor, where UAB designates group study rooms, tables, and computer stations for collaborative work.
cards.short_summary: A library-floor option for quietly collaborative work.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB Libraries permits group study on first-floor study rooms, tables, and computer stations when it does not disturb others.
cards.access_notes: Keep voices reasonable; close study-room doors because rooms are not soundproof.

cards.entity_name: Mervyn H. Sterne Library Third-Floor Quiet Zone
cards.title: Sterne Third-Floor Quiet Zone
cards.subtitle: Mervyn H. Sterne Library, third floor
cards.notes: Bring quiet, independent work to the third floor and use headphones for any audio; the whole floor remains designated as a quiet zone.
cards.short_summary: A designated quiet-library floor for focused work.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB states that the entire third floor of Sterne Library remains a quiet zone.
cards.source_title: Changes to Sterne Library's Quiet Zone
cards.access_notes: Minimize noise; the library’s room policy identifies the third floor as a quiet study area.

cards.entity_name: Mervyn H. Sterne Library Single Study Rooms
cards.title: Sterne Single Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Mervyn H. Sterne Library, third floor
cards.notes: Reserve a one-person room through the library portal, then check in at the HUB Service Desk; individual rooms can be booked for four hours.
cards.short_summary: Reservable, single-user rooms on Sterne’s third floor.
cards.evidence_claim: Sterne has 61 single rooms on the third floor; individual rooms may be booked for four hours with one renewal option.
cards.access_notes: Available to currently enrolled UAB students, postdocs, faculty, and staff with a UAB ONE Card; check in at the HUB Desk.

cards.entity_name: Mervyn H. Sterne Library Group Study Rooms
cards.title: Sterne Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Mervyn H. Sterne Library, first and third floors
cards.notes: Book a group room for a planned working session and arrive together at the HUB Desk; a group needs at least two people at checkout.
cards.short_summary: Reservable group rooms with a documented check-in process.
cards.evidence_claim: Sterne has 13 group study rooms, with nine on the first floor and four on the third floor.
cards.access_notes: Book online the same day or up to two weeks ahead; group-study bookings run three hours and require two group members at checkout.

cards.entity_name: Mervyn H. Sterne Library Study Carrels
cards.title: Sterne Study Carrels
cards.subtitle: Mervyn H. Sterne Library, third-floor quiet area
cards.notes: Use a carrel when you need a defined solo workspace; keep audio in headphones and maintain the minimal-noise expectations of the quiet area.
cards.short_summary: Individual carrels in Sterne’s quiet-study setting.
cards.evidence_claim: Sterne offers daily and long-term study carrels; carrels are limited to one person and the third floor is a quiet zone.
cards.access_notes: A valid UAB ID is required. Long-term carrels are for faculty, graduate students, and students with disabilities, subject to availability and application.

cards.title: SL 174 Collaborative Learning Room
cards.subtitle: Mervyn H. Sterne Library, Room SL 174
cards.notes: Request SL 174 for a larger collaborative session when eligible; its nine four-seat pods support table-based group work rather than silent solo study.
cards.short_summary: A reservable room with nine four-person learning pods.
cards.evidence_claim: SL 174 has nine pods of four seats for collaborative learning and may be used for collaborative group study during final exams.
cards.access_notes: Request through the library’s SL 174 reservation form; library instruction and Writing Center classes have priority.

cards.title: Sterne 385 Sensory Room
cards.subtitle: Mervyn H. Sterne Library, third floor
cards.notes: Reserve one of the two seats when a low-stimulation reset supports your work; return sensory items and furniture to their original places before leaving.
cards.short_summary: A reservable, calm setting with sensory-friendly equipment.
cards.evidence_claim: Sterne 385 is a reservable room for up to two users and includes adjustable lighting, a sound machine, meditation prompts, fidget tools, and weighted lap pads.
cards.source_title: See inside Sterne's new sensory room
cards.access_notes: Reservation required; it accommodates two independently reserved users and is intended as a calm, low-stimulation space rather than a traditional study room.

cards.entity_name: Lister Hill Library First-Floor Study Rooms
cards.title: Lister Hill First-Floor Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Lister Hill Library of the Health Sciences, first floor
cards.notes: Reserve a single or group room for a health-sciences study session, then check in at the HUB Service Desk before using the reserved space.
cards.short_summary: First-floor rooms for individual or collaborative sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: Lister Hill’s first floor has both group and single-person study rooms available for booking.
cards.source_title: Use this new interactive map feature to book study rooms, seminar rooms and other UAB Libraries spaces
cards.access_notes: For UAB community members; reserve online the same day or up to two weeks ahead, and check in at the Lister Hill HUB Desk.

cards.entity_name: Lister Hill Library Second-Floor Quiet Area
cards.title: Lister Hill Second-Floor Quiet Area
cards.subtitle: Lister Hill Library of the Health Sciences, second floor
cards.notes: Choose the second-floor quiet area for reading or concentrated drafting, and keep phone conversations outside or in a first-floor lobby area.
cards.short_summary: An open, quiet second-floor library environment.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB’s undergraduate catalog identifies a quiet area on level 2 among Lister Hill Library’s open study spaces.
cards.access_notes: Other library floors are designated quiet floors; use headphones for media and maintain a reasonable volume.

cards.entity_name: Lister Hill Library Second-Floor Conference Room
cards.title: Lister Hill Second-Floor Conference Room
cards.subtitle: Lister Hill Library of the Health Sciences, second floor
cards.notes: Use the space map to check this conference room’s availability, then reserve it for a planned group session that benefits from a dedicated room.
cards.short_summary: A bookable second-floor conference-room option.
cards.evidence_claim: Lister Hill Library has a conference room space available for booking on the second floor.
cards.source_title: Use this new interactive map feature to book study rooms, seminar rooms and other UAB Libraries spaces
cards.access_notes: Availability and reservation status are shown through the UAB Libraries interactive map and booking tools.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named, publicly documented destinations on practical campus-adjacent Birmingham corridors.

cards.title: Railroad Park
cards.subtitle: 1st Avenue South corridor
cards.notes: Enter from 1st Avenue South and use the park’s walking paths, gardens, play areas, and water features for a self-directed outdoor break.
cards.short_summary: A 19-acre public green space running along the railroad corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Railroad Park is a 19-acre greenspace on 1st Avenue South between 14th and 18th Streets, and public admission is free.
cards.access_notes: Open to the public daily, 7 a.m.–11 p.m.; the official site states there is no entrance fee.

cards.title: Regions Field
cards.subtitle: 1st Avenue South corridor
cards.notes: Check the Birmingham Barons schedule before going; the ballpark’s main public-facing location is on 1st Avenue South across from Railroad Park.
cards.short_summary: The downtown home field of the Birmingham Barons.
cards.evidence_claim: Regions Field, at 1401 1st Avenue South, is home to the Birmingham Barons and is in downtown’s Parkside District.
cards.access_notes: Game and event access depends on the published schedule and ticket availability.

cards.title: Negro Southern League Museum
cards.subtitle: 16th Street South corridor
cards.notes: Plan a daytime museum stop to explore Birmingham’s connection to Black baseball history; confirm the posted hours before travel.
cards.short_summary: A city museum focused on the Negro Southern League and Birmingham Black Barons.
cards.evidence_claim: The Negro Southern League Museum at 120 16th Street South presents the history and impact of African-American baseball.
cards.source_title: City of Birmingham — Negro Southern League Museum
cards.access_notes: The city lists museum hours Tuesday–Saturday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m.

cards.title: Red Mountain Theatre
cards.subtitle: 3rd Avenue South corridor
cards.notes: Look over the current program and choose a Mainstage or Discovery Theatre performance that fits your schedule before purchasing tickets.
cards.short_summary: A nonprofit performing-arts campus with two named theatres.
cards.evidence_claim: Red Mountain Theatre’s Arts Campus at 1600 3rd Avenue South includes the RMT Mainstage and the 133-seat Discovery Theatre.
cards.access_notes: Performance and box-office timing varies by production; consult the theatre’s current calendar.

cards.title: Alabama Theatre
cards.subtitle: 3rd Avenue North corridor
cards.notes: Use the theatre’s event calendar to select a film, concert, or live performance, then arrive via its documented 3rd Avenue North address.
cards.short_summary: A historic downtown venue presenting films and live performances.
cards.evidence_claim: The Alabama Theatre is at 1817 Third Avenue North and has presented movies, concerts, and live performances since 1927.
cards.access_notes: Events are individually scheduled; tickets are offered through the theatre’s event listings.

cards.title: McWane Science Center
cards.subtitle: 19th Street North corridor
cards.notes: Visit during daytime museum hours and use the center’s floor maps to plan exhibits and programming around the 2nd Avenue North corner.
cards.short_summary: A nonprofit science museum and research center in downtown Birmingham.
cards.evidence_claim: McWane Science Center is a science museum and research center at 200 19th Street North, on the corner of 2nd Avenue North.
cards.access_notes: Officially listed hours are weekdays 9 a.m.–5 p.m., Saturday 10 a.m.–5 p.m., and Sunday noon–5 p.m.

cards.title: Birmingham Civil Rights Institute
cards.subtitle: 16th Street North corridor
cards.notes: Set aside time for the institute’s galleries and use the 15th Street North entrance for the free parking described by the museum.
cards.short_summary: A museum destination within Birmingham’s Civil Rights District.
cards.evidence_claim: The Birmingham Civil Rights Institute is located at 520 16th Street North and provides parking access from 15th Street North.
cards.access_notes: Check the institute’s current tour hours and admissions information before visiting.

cards.title: Sixteenth Street Baptist Church
cards.subtitle: 6th Avenue North corridor
cards.notes: Use the church’s official contact details to arrange an appropriate visit, and treat this active congregation and historic site with care.
cards.short_summary: A named historic church in the Civil Rights District.
cards.evidence_claim: Sixteenth Street Baptist Church lists its address as 1530 6th Avenue North in Birmingham.
cards.access_notes: Hours and visitor arrangements are not verified here; contact the church directly before going.

cards.title: Kelly Ingram Park
cards.subtitle: 17th Street North corridor
cards.notes: Walk the park’s monument grounds at your own pace and pair it with nearby Civil Rights District sites for historical context.
cards.short_summary: A city park whose monuments commemorate Birmingham civil-rights history.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Birmingham identifies Kelly Ingram Park as a Civil Rights Movement battleground with monuments recognizing its history.
cards.access_notes: A City of Birmingham event notice places the park at 500 17th Street North and 5th Avenue North.

cards.title: Birmingham Public Library — Central
cards.subtitle: Park Place corridor
cards.notes: Bring a research question or browse the Central Library’s archives, manuscripts, and subject departments during its posted public service hours.
cards.short_summary: The central branch of Birmingham’s public-library system, with archives and research collections.
cards.evidence_claim: Birmingham Public Library’s Central location is at 2100 Park Place and includes Archives and Manuscripts, arts, business, and other departments.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: Monday and Wednesday–Saturday 9 a.m.–6 p.m.; Tuesday 9 a.m.–8 p.m.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented UAB customs, campus events, and Blazer-spirit practices.

cards.title: The Gurney Derby
cards.subtitle: Annual UAB team gurney race
cards.notes: Form a team or watch the race: participants costume a “patient” and move a gurney through this annual UAB event.
cards.short_summary: A playful UAB race built around decorated teams, gurneys, and imaginative passengers.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB identifies the Gurney Derby as an annual tradition in which student teams race a gurney carrying a themed “patient.”
cards.access_notes: Check UAB Student Affairs and Homecoming announcements for the current event schedule and participation details.

cards.entity_name: UAB Homecoming Building Decoration and Spirit Competition
cards.title: Decorate, Sing, and Shout for Homecoming
cards.subtitle: UAB Homecoming tradition
cards.notes: Visit during Homecoming to see groups decorate buildings and perform chants and songs for the campus competition.
cards.short_summary: Homecoming turns campus buildings into a backdrop for decorated displays and spirit performances.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB describes Homecoming as a tradition featuring building decoration plus singing and shouting while judges evaluate entries.
cards.access_notes: Events and competition access vary by the annual Homecoming schedule.

cards.title: Into the Streets
cards.subtitle: UAB community-service tradition
cards.notes: Join a listed project when registration opens and plan to work alongside students, faculty, and staff in Birmingham.
cards.short_summary: A UAB service day connecting the campus community with Birmingham projects.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB describes Into the Streets as a tradition where students, faculty, and staff complete service projects in Birmingham.
cards.access_notes: Participation requires an announced project and any registration instructions from UAB.

cards.title: Blazer Splash
cards.subtitle: Campus Green water-balloon event
cards.notes: Bring clothes suited to getting wet and follow event guidance for the water-balloon activities on the Campus Green.
cards.short_summary: A large UAB water-play gathering with balloons, slides, and other splash activities.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB describes Blazer Splash as a Campus Green event with 15,000 water balloons, water slides, water shooters, a dunking booth, and slip n’ slides.
cards.access_notes: Attend only when scheduled; wear appropriate footwear and follow event-staff instructions around wet activity areas.

cards.title: International Festival
cards.subtitle: UAB cultural celebration
cards.notes: Come ready to sample offered foods, learn about cultural traditions, and watch the program’s live performances.
cards.short_summary: A UAB gathering that pairs cultural exploration with food and live performance.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB describes International Festival as a chance to try foods, explore cultural traditions, and enjoy live performance.
cards.access_notes: Food availability and event timing depend on the current program.

cards.title: Blazer Showdown
cards.subtitle: Homecoming talent-show tradition
cards.notes: See the Homecoming performance program at Alys Stephens Center and arrive in time for the participating skits and dances.
cards.short_summary: UAB’s Homecoming stage showcase for elaborate skits and dance performances.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB identifies Blazer Showdown as a Homecoming tradition of student talent, including skits and dance performances at Alys Stephens Performing Arts Center.
cards.access_notes: Consult the annual Homecoming program for ticketing or entry requirements.

cards.title: Be Seen in Green
cards.subtitle: Friday Blazer-spirit practice
cards.notes: Wear a green UAB shirt on the designated Friday and pair it with another campus event or class-day photo.
cards.short_summary: A simple Friday practice for visibly showing UAB spirit in green.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB Student Affairs lists wearing a UAB shirt on “Be Seen in Green” day among its UAB traditions.
cards.source_title: 50 things to do at UAB — UAB Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: No special access is required; use an item of green UAB apparel you already have.

cards.title: The Camille Armstrong Step Show
cards.subtitle: UAB step-show tradition
cards.notes: Watch for the event announcement, then attend the scheduled show to experience this recurring UAB performance tradition.
cards.short_summary: A named UAB step show included in the university’s traditions list.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB Student Affairs lists the Camille Armstrong Step Show among the events every Blazer should attend.
cards.access_notes: Check the current Student Affairs calendar for date, location, and any admission details.

cards.title: Diningopoly
cards.subtitle: UAB dining-themed campus event
cards.notes: Look for the current event listing and follow its activity instructions; it is one of the recurring UAB events Student Affairs highlights.
cards.short_summary: A named dining-themed event that appears on UAB’s list of campus traditions.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB Student Affairs includes Diningopoly in its list of events every Blazer should attend.
cards.access_notes: Refer to the current event announcement for timing, location, and participation requirements.

cards.entity_name: Fried Chicken Thursday at The Commons
cards.title: Fried Chicken Thursday
cards.subtitle: The Commons dining tradition
cards.notes: Visit The Commons on the designated Thursday and confirm the day’s menu before planning a meal around this listed campus custom.
cards.short_summary: A weekly dining custom at The Commons recognized on UAB’s traditions checklist.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB Student Affairs lists eating at The Commons for Fried Chicken Thursday among its UAB traditions.
cards.source_title: 50 things to do at UAB — UAB Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: A meal plan, payment, or guest access may be required; verify the current menu and dining access before visiting.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of Alabama at Birmingham, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key, under-21-safe first-weekend route that starts on campus and branches into Birmingham’s public cultural and outdoor places.

cards.title: Start by getting oriented on the Campus Green
cards.subtitle: First stop · UAB’s central outdoor green space
cards.notes: Walk the sidewalks around the Green to locate the Recreation Center, Dining Commons, residence halls, and University Boulevard before making other plans.
cards.short_summary: Use the central lawn as an easy visual anchor for your first campus walk.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB describes the Campus Green as an open space bounded by University Boulevard, the Recreation Center, Dining Commons, residence halls, and other campus buildings.
cards.source_title: Campus Green | University of Alabama at Birmingham
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus green space; check the university calendar for scheduled events.

cards.title: Make the Hill your indoor reset point
cards.subtitle: Second stop · 1400 University Blvd.
cards.notes: Use the building map or information desk to find dining, the bookstore, student services, and reservable spaces; confirm weekend hours before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A practical campus hub for meals, information, and a break indoors.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB describes the Hill Student Center as a communal place with meals, books, student services, meetings, and activities.
cards.source_title: Hill Student Center | University of Alabama at Birmingham
cards.access_notes: The official page lists abbreviated summer hours; schedules can change.

cards.title: Check the dining map for Magic City Eats
cards.subtitle: Meal stop · UAB Campus Dining
cards.notes: Look up the current campus dining map and hours, then choose Magic City Eats if it is operating during your visit and its location fits your route.
cards.short_summary: A named UAB Campus Dining option to check when planning a campus meal.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB Campus Dining identifies Magic City Eats as one of its dining locations and provides a locations-and-hours page.
cards.access_notes: Consult UAB Dining’s current locations-and-hours page before going; food requires purchase or an eligible dining balance.

cards.title: Tour the Campus Recreation Center
cards.subtitle: Active afternoon · 1501 University Blvd.
cards.notes: Bring your ONE Card if you are an eligible UAB student, then pick one facility feature to try or simply get familiar with the building next to the Green.
cards.short_summary: A campus recreation facility with courts, aquatics, fitness space, and more.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB says currently enrolled students have Recreation Center access included in tuition and identifies the center at 1501 University Boulevard.
cards.source_title: Student Services & Facilities | UAB Undergraduate Catalog
cards.access_notes: Eligible UAB students should bring a ONE Card; facility access and program availability are subject to university policies.

cards.title: Try the climbing wall if you have member access
cards.subtitle: Active option · Campus Recreation Center mezzanine
cards.notes: Ask Recreation staff about current wall access, required instruction, and equipment before climbing; choose the bouldering wall or a scheduled program that fits your comfort.
cards.short_summary: A structured, on-campus climbing option within the Recreation Center.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB documents a 36-foot climbing wall and a 12-foot bouldering wall in the Campus Recreation Center, open to URec members.
cards.source_title: Student Services & Facilities | UAB Undergraduate Catalog
cards.access_notes: Access is for URec members; ask staff about current wall hours, requirements, and programming.

cards.title: Set aside a quiet stop at Sterne Library
cards.subtitle: Campus pause · 917 13th St. S.
cards.notes: Use the library as a calm place to review the weekend, find a study seat, or ask at a service point; check its current weekend hours before arriving.
cards.short_summary: A named UAB library stop with published visitor-access guidance.
cards.evidence_claim: UAB’s library access guidelines state that non-UAB visitors may access Sterne Library during library open hours and list Saturday hours of 9 a.m.–5 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Visitor access is limited to library open hours; verify the current calendar and any access requirements before visiting.

cards.title: Take an evening walk at Railroad Park
cards.subtitle: Off-campus outdoor stop · Birmingham
cards.notes: Use the park’s posted entrances and paths for an easy outdoor stretch, then head out before closing; keep any route and transport plan simple and daylight-aware.
cards.short_summary: A public Birmingham park with long daily hours and no entrance fee.
cards.evidence_claim: Railroad Park states that it is open daily from 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. and has no entrance fee.
cards.access_notes: Officially open 7 a.m.–11 p.m. daily; the park advises using its entrances and provides parking guidance.

cards.title: Continue along Rotary Trail
cards.subtitle: Downtown connector · four-block walking/running/biking path
cards.notes: Use the trail for a short, self-paced connection between downtown landmarks; yield to other users and turn back if your group’s daylight or transport plan changes.
cards.short_summary: A landscaped downtown trail that links Railroad Park toward Sloss Furnaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The Birmingham Rotary Club describes Rotary Trail as a four-block walking, running, and biking path that connects Railroad Park and Sloss Furnaces.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public trail; plan a return route and follow posted conditions.

cards.title: See Birmingham’s industrial history at Sloss Furnaces
cards.subtitle: Weekend culture stop · 20th Street North area
cards.notes: Take the self-guided route through the historic site, pause at the interpretive features, and verify the day’s hours before leaving campus for this destination.
cards.short_summary: A preserved industrial landmark with free general admission and self-guided touring.
cards.evidence_claim: Sloss Furnaces states that admission is free, self-guided tours are available, and normal weekend hours are Saturday 10 a.m.–4 p.m. and Sunday noon–4 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Official normal hours list Saturday 10 a.m.–4 p.m. and Sunday noon–4 p.m.; guided or special tours may carry a fee.

cards.title: Finish with a gallery visit at Birmingham Museum of Art
cards.subtitle: Downtown cultural stop · 2000 Reverend Abraham Woods Jr. Blvd.
cards.notes: Choose a few collection galleries rather than trying to cover everything, and check the museum calendar for closures or exhibition-specific ticketing before you travel downtown.
cards.short_summary: A downtown art museum whose general admission covers collection galleries and most exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: The Birmingham Museum of Art says general admission is free every day and includes collection galleries and most exhibitions unless otherwise noted.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | Birmingham Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Hours vary by day, and the official page notes planned closures and possible exhibition exceptions; confirm before visiting.
